questions.prompt: Which features does Growth add on top of the core platform?

options.text: Class booking, memberships, point of sale and reports
Leads, sequences, ads manager, referrals and reviews
The AI agent that answers and books from the inbox
The branded app and the library for on-demand video

questions.reveal: Core runs the business. Growth adds the marketing suite. The AI agent and the add-ons sit on top.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks what Spot Filler does. What’s accurate?

options.text: It lets clients pick their own spot from a room map at checkout
It lists open spots on a marketplace other studios’ clients see
It moves the next waitlisted client in when someone cancels
It messages past attendees of that class type when it isn’t full

questions.reveal: Spot Filler targets clients who’ve taken that kind of class before. Spot selection on a room map is a different feature, and AEs have mixed the two up.

questions.prompt: Midway through a demo, a prospect asks what her total would be with the marketing suite and on-demand video. What do you do?

options.text: Build that package in the calculator and show her the total
Add the two prices from memory so the demo keeps moving
Tell her you’ll email a quote once you’ve worked it out
Give a range from the lowest to the highest plan for now

questions.reveal: Building it live takes a minute and gives a number you can stand behind.

questions.prompt: The prospect’s co-owner missed the demo. She wants something to show him what’s in each plan. What’s best?

options.text: Write him an email listing the features you remember
Send the recording and tell him to skip to the pricing
Download the calculator’s comparison sheet for both plans
Send him your pricing slide with a few notes added on top

questions.reveal: The comparison sheet lists every feature in each plan side by side, and it matches the quote.

questions.prompt: In discovery, a prospect on MindBody tells you her monthly fee. What’s the most useful follow-up?

options.text: Ask if she’d pay a bit more for a lot more value
Ask when she’d like to see our pricing on this call
Ask what that fee includes, like marketing or an app
Ask how happy she is with MindBody from one to ten

questions.reveal: Knowing what her fee covers lets you build a like-for-like package and compare fairly.

questions.prompt: Why ask about current spend before you show any price?

options.text: So the price lands next to a number they already pay
So you can set your quote just under what they pay now
So you know whether to offer free months at the close
So you can cut discovery short if the budget is too low

questions.reveal: The current total is the anchor. You still build the quote in the calculator; you don’t set it to undercut.

questions.prompt: A spa pays one tool for booking and a second tool for texting and reviews. How do you compare costs?

options.text: Compare our price with the booking tool only, since that’s the switch
Leave the texting tool out, since she may keep it after switching
Compare with whichever of the two tools costs her more each month
Add both tools together and compare with the matching package

questions.reveal: When Momence replaces two tools, the fair comparison is against both of them.

questions.prompt: You’ve shown pricing and the prospect goes quiet. You never asked what she pays now. What’s the best recovery?

options.text: Offer a discount right away to get past the sticker shock
Ask what she pays today in total, then compare the two
Move on to onboarding so price doesn’t stall the call
Explain how the features pay for themselves within a year

questions.reveal: It’s late, but the anchor still helps. Get her total, then compare like for like.

questions.prompt: What does a branded app give a studio that the free Momence app doesn’t?

options.text: The studio’s own name and logo in the App Store
Booking features clients can’t get in the free app
A way to stop clients seeing other studios’ ads
Push notifications to clients about new classes

questions.reveal: The layout and features are the same. The branded app puts the studio’s name on the phone.

questions.prompt: A one-location studio asks for a branded app because “clients like having an app.” What’s your best move?

options.text: Add the branded app since she asked, and move on to marketing
Tell her the branded app is a waste of money at one location
Show the free app first, then ask what branding would add for her
Offer the branded app for free so it won’t affect her decision

questions.reveal: Her clients get an app either way. Let her decide if the name and logo are worth the cost.

questions.prompt: A prospect with two locations asks if video on demand is charged per location. You’re not sure. What do you say?

options.text: That it’s charged once, since most add-ons work that way
That you’ll confirm it and get back to her by a set time
That it’s per location, so she isn’t surprised later on
That it comes with Growth, so it won’t matter for her

questions.reveal: Per-location charging for on-demand is still being confirmed. Saying when you’ll answer beats a guess.

questions.prompt: A studio is adding a second location under the same brand. How is it usually set up?

options.text: Each location gets its own dashboard and its own login
The second location opens a separate account and plan
Both share one schedule, with no filter by location
Both run from one dashboard, filtered by location

questions.reveal: Same-brand locations share a dashboard. Different brands use separate dashboards you switch between.

questions.prompt: An owner says she’s at capacity with waitlists on most classes, and asks if she needs Growth. What do you do?

options.text: Recommend Growth, since every studio benefits from more leads
Quote Growth and the AI agent so she has room to grow later
Tell her flatly that she has no use for marketing right now
Ask what she wants from marketing, then build what fits her

questions.reveal: A full studio may still want reviews or win-back, or may not. Her answer decides the build.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks, “Do I really need Growth?” Which question helps you most?

options.text: “Where do new clients come from, and what happens to leads?”
“Could you fit Growth into your monthly budget right now?”
“Have studios you know picked Growth, or just the core?”
“Do you want to see every feature before you decide?”

questions.reveal: Lead flow shows whether the marketing suite would earn its cost for this studio.

questions.prompt: A prospect comparing Arketa asks why Momence costs more. Which answer keeps her trust?

options.text: “Arketa is cheaper because it has about half our software.”
“Arketa was built by ex-staff who copied our design.”
“Arketa does a lot well. Let me show what our price adds.”
“Arketa will raise prices once you’re in their contract.”

questions.reveal: The other three are unverified knocks. A prospect who checks one will doubt everything else you said.

questions.prompt: Which point is fair to make when comparing Arketa’s checkout with Momence’s?

options.text: Arketa can’t pass card fees on to clients at checkout
Momence doesn’t make a new client create a password
Arketa has no way to book a guest along with yourself
Arketa doesn’t let clients buy packs during checkout

questions.reveal: The side-by-side showed Arketa asking for a password. Arketa can pass on fees and book guests, so don’t claim those.

questions.prompt: Which of these can you offer without your manager’s approval?

options.text: The package price the calculator shows
A small discount to close a deal this week
An extra free month for a pre-open studio
A free branded app for the first year

questions.reveal: The calculator quote is yours to give. Discounts, free months and free add-ons need approval.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks what her price will be when the contract renews. You don’t know the policy. What do you say?

options.text: That prices have never gone up, so she has nothing to worry about
That you’ll confirm with your manager and reply by a set time
That it renews at the same rate, since most contracts work that way
That she can renegotiate at renewal if she’s unhappy with the rate

questions.reveal: Renewal terms are still being confirmed. A promise you can’t back up can follow you into the contract.

questions.prompt: Your manager approved a free branded app for a year as a contract addendum. The prospect asks what it costs after year one. What do you do?

options.text: Say it will most likely stay free, since that was the intent
Quote the branded app price you heard in your last demo
Check with your manager and get it written into the addendum
Tell her not to worry about it, since it’s a year away

questions.reveal: Whatever happens after year one should be in writing, approved by the manager who gave the addendum.

questions.prompt: On a call, a prospect asks for a lower price. You think your manager would agree. What’s the strongest move?

options.text: Promise it now, since you’re confident it’ll be approved
Tell her the price is fixed, to avoid setting expectations
End the call and email her a new price later in the week
Ask your manager during the call if you can, then confirm it

questions.reveal: Approval on the call keeps momentum and keeps the number real.
